findings.text: Scheduler suspend and resume hooks preserve per-task temporary high memory mappings across context switch by clearing them on exit and reinstalling the same stored entries on entry, operating on the current task control and the initial address space with architecture specific slot translation and unmap and map notifications.
Fork helper enforces that a new task starts with no active temporary mappings, diagnosing a nonzero count and resetting the control block to a clean state.
Boot time initializer prepares the persistent mapping hash table for use, making every bucket list empty and every bucket lock usable.
Public page table walk entry validates the callback table before delegating to the core walker that iterates address ranges across virtual areas and invokes hole, test and level handlers.
Heterogeneous memory walk dispatch binds handlers for upper, middle and hole levels plus huge entries and eligibility testing, always executed under a read oriented walk lock.
Upper level and huge entry handling is configuration dependent, with one build providing full handlers and another build disabling them by exposing no handler.

Persistent mapping record associates a page descriptor with its temporary virtual address and links records together for hash bucket membership; a static pool sized by the permanent map limit holds all records.
Hash bucket combines a membership list with its own protecting spin lock, aligned to avoid sharing cache lines in symmetric multiprocessing builds, replicated for every hash value.

Heterogeneous memory walk cursor carries the target range descriptor, an optional flag reporting whether the caller lock was dropped, progress markers for the current fault window, and the accumulated fault requirement.
Persistent mapping hash order is seven, denoting one hundred twenty eight buckets indexed by the low hash bits.
Internal walk control uses negative EAGAIN to mean a fault window was recorded and needs handling outside the walk, and negative ENOLCK to mean the caller lock was dropped during that handling.

Fault need encoding uses bit zero for a basic fault, bit one for a write fault, and their union for the full requirement; a separate mask preserves only direct memory access mapping attributes across output fills.

Temporary mapping suspend and resume honor a debug discipline where alternating positions act as unmapped guards that must stay empty, skip empty stored entries with a one time diagnostic, and otherwise translate each logical position plus stored frame into a fixed address before touching its entry.

Whether a page needs faulting blends per entry request bits filtered by an allowed mask with range wide defaults, requiring no action without a fault request, demanding write handling when writability is requested but absent, and demanding a basic fault when validity is absent.

Output array updates preserve caller owned mapping attributes while replacing address and status portions with freshly derived values, applied uniformly to single entries, contiguous runs and error or empty encodings.

Unmapped holes outside any virtual area fail when faulting was requested and otherwise report a per page error; holes inside a virtual area record a fault window when needed and otherwise report empty.

Translation from hardware entries to portable status treats absent, nonpresent and protection none encodings as no information and otherwise reports validity plus writability together with a size order derived from the level shift.

Device private entries owned by the requesting owner are reported directly with appropriate writability without faulting, while foreign private, swap like and exclusive encodings trigger fault recording when faulting is requested; migration encodings cause a wait and a busy retry after releasing maps.
One configuration for absent middle entries and corrupted middle entries cannot satisfy a fault request and fails, otherwise filling the span with a per page error marker.
Only readable ordinary memory areas are walked; device or direct frame areas and unreadable areas fail when faulting is requested, otherwise fill an error and are skipped without descending.
Huge and large leaf mappings are expanded into per page outputs with a shared size order, preserving mapping attributes and adding consecutive frame numbers from the leaf base plus span offset.

Empty entries and write protection markers for user fault handling are treated as needing evaluation for fault recording rather than as present data, with unmapping performed before leaving the table handler on fault or error paths.
Each persistent mapping hash bucket is guarded by its own spin lock protecting only that bucket list, with all locks and lists initialized during early boot before any use.

Upper leaf inspection holds the transparent huge lock across the read and either records a fault or expands outputs before release, while huge entries hold the huge entry lock across the same decision; middle level scanning is lockless and relies on external invalidation notification.

Page walking requires the address space lock in the mode declared by the callback table plus per area locking when inside an area, asserts the caller holds the address space lock for the heterogeneous range fault path, and treats positive test results as a skip signal never propagated to callers.

Range faulting repeats walk then external fault handling until stable: a recorded window invokes the fault handler outside table locks, busy or interval invalidation restarts from the recorded progress with earlier outputs committed and later inputs untouched, lock loss becomes busy unless a fatal signal requires interruption, and other errors terminate.

External fault handling looks up the containing area, rejects write faults against unwritable areas, faults each page remotely with retry permission when the caller tracks lock loss, and converts completion or retry indications into a lock lost signal while mapping hardware error encodings to negative errno values.

Core walking partitions the requested span at area boundaries, reporting gaps with no area through the hole path, testing each covered area for skip or abort, descending into tables on success, and stopping at the first error while normalizing control positives to success.

Middle level reads are performed without holding the table lock with a second read to confirm huge state after a potential concurrent split, depending on external invalidation callbacks for correctness rather than mutual exclusion.

Slot position for suspend and resume is recomputed from logical order and stored frame number rather than from a stored address, a workaround for cache colouring on one architecture that is expected to fold away elsewhere but miscomputes if the derivation disagrees with the original mapping.

Entries that are neither ordinary memory nor the shared zero frame are surfaced as errors when no fault is needed but cause a hard failure when faulting was requested, so callers must not request faulting over such mappings.
